descriptionChirho: A young child, infant, or small boy/girl; the diminutive of παῖς used throughout the Gospels for Jesus as an infant (Matt 2:8-14; Luke 2:17, 27, 40), for children brought to Jesus (Matt 18:2-5; 19:13-14; Mark 10:15), and as a term of endearment for disciples (1 John 2:18). Multilingual evidence is uniform across number: Spanish 'niño/niños', Hindi 'बालक/बच्चे', Arabic 'طِفْل/أَوْلَاد', Korean '아이/아이들', Swahili 'mtoto/watoto'. The singular cluster (S73700) and plural cluster (S73701) are purely grammatical number variants of the same lexical sense — a young child or infant — not semantically distinct meanings.
